objects.definition:
typedef enum {
	WGET_E_SUCCESS = 0, /* OK */
	WGET_E_UNKNOWN = -1, /* general error if nothing else appropriate */
	WGET_E_MEMORY = -2, /* memory allocation failure */
	WGET_E_INVALID = -3, /* invalid value to function */
	WGET_E_TIMEOUT = -4, /* timeout condition */
	WGET_E_CONNECT = -5, /* connect failure */
	WGET_E_HANDSHAKE = -6, /* general TLS handshake failure */
	WGET_E_CERTIFICATE = -7, /* general TLS certificate failure */
	WGET_E_TLS_DISABLED = -8, /* TLS was not enabled at compile time */
	WGET_E_XML_PARSE_ERR = -9, /* XML parsing failed */
	WGET_E_OPEN = -10, /* Failed to open file */
	WGET_E_IO = -11, /* General I/O error (read/write/stat/...) */
	WGET_E_UNSUPPORTED = -12, /* Unsupported function */
} wget_error;
objects.description: Library-wide error code enumeration used by libwget APIs. Negative values indicate errors; zero is success.
Opaque double-linked list container type. Elements are managed via libwget list functions.
Opaque bitmap structure storing a dynamic bitset; manipulated via wget_bitmap_* APIs.

objects.definition:
typedef struct {
	char *
		data; //!< pointer to internal memory
	size_t
		length; //!< number of bytes in 'data'
	size_t
		size; //!< capacity of 'data' (terminating 0 byte doesn't count here)
	bool
		release_data : 1, //!< 'data' has been malloc'ed and must be freed
		release_buf : 1, //!< wget_buffer structure has been malloc'ed and must be freed
		error : 1; //!< a memory failure occurred, the result in 'data' is likely erroneous
} wget_buffer;
objects.description: Growable byte buffer with length/capacity and ownership flags; used throughout for building strings and payloads.
Opaque logger instance used by libwget’s logging subsystem.
Opaque dynamic array storing void* elements with optional comparator and destructor; many subsystems use it.
Opaque hash map mapping keys to values; stringmap is a specialized alias.
Opaque iterator over hashmap/stringmap entries.
Alias of wget_hashmap specialized for string keys; created via stringmap-specific constructors.
Opaque thread handle for libwget thread wrapper.
Opaque mutex handle used with wget_thread_* APIs.
Opaque condition variable handle used with thread wrappers.
Opaque decompressor context used to decode various content-encodings and stream data to a sink callback.

objects.definition:

objects.description: Enumeration of supported HTTP content-encodings for decompression.
Scheme indicator for IRIs/URLs: http or https.
Parsed URI/IRI structure holding split components, scheme/port, and allocation flags. Managed via wget_iri_* functions.
Opaque cookie database used to store and retrieve HTTP cookies.
Opaque cookie entry representation parsed from Set-Cookie and stored in cookie DB.
Opaque HSTS database for Strict-Transport-Security policy storage; pluggable via vtable.
Vtable of function pointers to implement a custom HSTS database plugin.
Opaque HPKP database for storing Public-Key-Pins entries; pluggable via vtable.
Opaque HPKP entry corresponding to a Public-Key-Pins header.
Vtable of function pointers to implement a custom HPKP database plugin.
Opaque TLS session cache entry for session resumption.
Opaque TLS session database managing cached TLS sessions.
Opaque OCSP cache/database for revocation status; pluggable via vtable.
Vtable of function pointers to implement a custom OCSP database plugin. Note: load/save names appear swapped in structure; follow API docs when implementing.
Opaque container for .netrc entries.
Single .netrc credential entry with host, login, password, and optional port.
Result item from CSS parsing describing one discovered URL and metadata.
Lightweight pointer+length string view used in parsers.

objects.definition:
typedef struct {
	wget_string
		url; //!< URL within the parsed document (pointer and length)
	wget_string
		download; //!< Value of additional 'download' attribute, the name to be saved to disk
	char
		attr[16]; //!< name of the attribute containing the URL, e.g. 'href'
	char
		tag[16]; //!< name of the HTML tag containing the URL, e.g. 'a'
	bool
		link_inline : 1; //!< 1 = rel was 'stylesheet' or 'shortcut icon'
} wget_html_parsed_url;
objects.description: Record describing a URL reference found in HTML along with tag/attribute context.
Aggregate result from HTML parsing including discovered URLs, encoding, base, and flags.
Descriptor for an HTML tag and optional attribute filter used when parsing.

objects.definition: typedef void wget_xml_callback(void *, int, const char *, const char *, const char *, size_t, size_t);
objects.description: Callback signature invoked by XML/HTML parsers for tokens, attributes, and content. Pointer form denotes function pointer type.
Opaque DNS cache storing resolved addrinfo entries.
Opaque DNS resolver handle providing async/sync resolution and caching hooks.
Opaque TCP connection/session handle wrapping sockets and optional TLS.
Parsed name/value parameter pair used in HTTP headers.
Parsed HTTP Link header item with relation, type, priority, and target URI.
Parsed Digest header entry containing algorithm and base64 digest.
Parsed authentication challenge (WWW-Authenticate/Proxy-Authenticate) with scheme and parameters.
HTTP transfer-encoding indicator: identity or chunked.
HTTP response object holding parsed headers, body buffer, status, metadata, and parsed helper vectors.
Opaque HTTP connection/session abstraction over TCP/TLS handling protocol details.

objects.definition:
typedef struct {
	wget_vector *
		headers; //!< list of HTTP headers
	const char *
		body; //!< body data to be sent or NULL
	wget_http_header_callback
		*header_callback; //!< called after HTTP header has been received
	wget_http_body_callback
		*body_callback; //!< called for each body data packet received
	void *
		user_data; //!< user data for the request (used by async application code)
	void *
		header_user_data; //!< meant to be used in header callback function
	void *
		body_user_data; //!< meant to be used in body callback function
	wget_buffer
		esc_resource; //!< URI escaped resource
	wget_buffer
		esc_host; //!< URI escaped host
	size_t
		body_length; //!< length of the body data
	int32_t
		stream_id; //!< HTTP2 stream id
	wget_iri_scheme
		scheme; //!< scheme of the request for proxied connections
	char
		esc_resource_buf[256]; //!< static buffer used by esc_resource (avoids mallocs)
	char
		esc_host_buf[64]; //!< static buffer used by esc_host (avoids mallocs)
	char
		method[8]; //!< currently we just need HEAD, GET and POST
	bool
		response_keepheader : 1; //!< the application wants the response header data
	bool
		response_ignorelength : 1; //!< ignore the Content-Length in the response header
	bool
		debug_skip_body : 1; //!< if set, do not print the request body (e.g. because it's binary)
	long long
		request_start; //!< When this request was sent out
	long long
		first_response_start; //!< The time we read the first bytes back

} wget_http_request;
objects.description: HTTP request object containing headers, optional body, callbacks, buffers for escaped components, and flags.
Opaque handle for incremental hashing (digest) operations.

objects.description: Enumeration of supported digest algorithms for hash routines.
Descriptor of a single Metalink mirror endpoint with priority and location.
Hash type+value entry used by Metalink metadata.
Metalink piece checksum covering a file segment with position and length.
Top-level Metalink document representation for a file, including mirrors and checksums.
Opaque structure holding parsed robots.txt data including allowed paths and sitemaps.
Enum selecting progress speed display unit (bytes or bits).
Opaque progress bar manager for multi-slot download progress display.
Enum of console foreground colors for logging/output.
Plugin handle passed to plugin entry points; holds plugin-specific data and a vtable provided by core.
Action record used by URL filter plugins to communicate accept/reject or alternative actions.
Handle representing a downloaded file exposed to plugins for inspection/post-processing.
Vtable implemented by libwget core; plugins call methods via this to interact with wget2.
Statistics payload reported for DNS resolutions.
Statistics payload for OCSP validation results.
Statistics payload for TLS connections including timing, protocol and session attributes.
Enum for HPKP verification result reported in stats callbacks.
Enum selecting output format for stats reporting.

functions.name: wget_strerror
functions.description: Maps a wget_error code to a human-readable constant string. Use to log or display libwget error codes.
requirements: Argument err must be a valid wget_error enum value.

functions.name: wget_global_init
functions.description: Initializes or configures libwget global settings keyed by integer constants (e.g., WGET_DEBUG_STREAM, WGET_COOKIE_DB). Variadic value(s) depend on the key.
requirements: key must be one of the defined WGET_* keys for global initialization.
Variadic arguments must match the expected type for the provided key (unknown from header).
Should be called before using related global features.

functions.name: wget_global_deinit
functions.description: Deinitializes libwget global state configured via wget_global_init.

functions.name: wget_global_get_ptr
functions.description: Retrieves a pointer global value for a given key previously set via wget_global_init.
requirements: key must be a key whose value type is a pointer.

functions.name: wget_global_get_int
functions.description: Retrieves an integer global value for a given key previously set via wget_global_init.
requirements: key must be a key whose value type is an int.

functions.name: wget_global_get_func
functions.description: Retrieves a function-pointer global value for a given key previously set via wget_global_init.
requirements: key must be a key whose value type is wget_global_func*.

functions.name: wget_ready_2_read
functions.description: Tests if a file descriptor is readable within timeout milliseconds. Returns readiness status (unknown exact convention).
requirements: fd must be a valid file descriptor.
timeout is in milliseconds; negative/zero behavior unknown.

functions.name: wget_ready_2_write
functions.description: Tests if a file descriptor is writable within timeout milliseconds. Returns readiness status (unknown exact convention).
requirements: fd must be a valid file descriptor.
timeout is in milliseconds; negative/zero behavior unknown.

functions.name: wget_ready_2_transfer
functions.signature: int wget_ready_2_transfer(int fd, int timeout, int mode);
functions.description: Checks a file descriptor for IO readiness according to mode flags (WGET_IO_READABLE/WGET_IO_WRITABLE) within timeout milliseconds.
requirements: fd must be a valid file descriptor.
mode is a bitmask of WGET_IO_READABLE and/or WGET_IO_WRITABLE.
timeout is in milliseconds; negative/zero behavior unknown.

functions.name: wget_strcmp
functions.description: Compares two C strings (likely strcmp-like semantics). Marked pure.
requirements: s1 and s2 may be NULL or non-NULL (no nonnull attribute specified). Passing NULL is likely invalid but unspecified.

functions.name: wget_strcasecmp
functions.description: Case-insensitive string compare using current locale or library rules. Marked pure.

functions.name: wget_strcasecmp_ascii
functions.description: ASCII-only case-insensitive string comparison. Marked pure.

functions.name: wget_strncasecmp_ascii
functions.signature: int wget_strncasecmp_ascii(const char *s1, const char *s2, size_t n);
functions.description: ASCII-only case-insensitive comparison of up to n bytes. Marked pure.
requirements: n is the maximum number of characters to compare.

functions.name: wget_strtolower
functions.description: Lowercases a string in place and returns s.
requirements: s must point to writable, NUL-terminated memory.

functions.name: wget_strncmp
functions.signature: int wget_strncmp(const char *s1, const char *s2, size_t n);
functions.description: Compares two strings up to n characters (likely strcmp semantics). Marked pure.
requirements: n is the maximum number of characters to compare.

functions.name: wget_strncasecmp
functions.signature: int wget_strncasecmp(const char *s1, const char *s2, size_t n);
functions.description: Case-insensitive compare up to n characters. Marked pure.
requirements: n is the maximum number of characters to compare.

functions.name: wget_memtohex
functions.signature: void wget_memtohex(const unsigned char * __restrict src, size_t src_len, char * __restrict dst, size_t dst_size);
functions.description: Converts binary memory to a lowercase hex string into dst, including terminator if space permits.
requirements: src points to at least src_len bytes.
dst points to a writable buffer of size dst_size.
Caller must ensure dst_size is sufficient for output (typically 2*src_len + 1 for NUL), exact requirement not documented.

functions.name: wget_millisleep
functions.description: Sleeps the current thread for ms milliseconds.
requirements: ms is a sleep duration in milliseconds; negative behavior unknown.

functions.name: wget_get_timemillis
functions.description: Returns a timestamp in milliseconds (epoch or monotonic origin unspecified).

functions.name: wget_percent_unescape
functions.description: In-place percent-decoding of a URL-encoded string. Returns status (exact convention not documented).
requirements: src must point to writable, NUL-terminated memory.

functions.name: wget_match_tail
functions.description: Checks if string s ends with tail (case-sensitive). Returns an int status (likely boolean). Marked pure and nonnull.
requirements: s must be non-NULL.
tail must be non-NULL.

functions.name: wget_match_tail_nocase
functions.description: Checks if string s ends with tail (case-insensitive). Returns int status. Marked pure and nonnull.
requirements: s must be non-NULL.
tail must be non-NULL.

functions.name: wget_strnglob
functions.signature: char *wget_strnglob(const char *str, size_t n, int flags);
functions.description: Performs a glob-like match/transformation on the first n bytes of str and returns a newly allocated string or NULL on failure. Details and flags are not documented in this header.
requirements: str may be NULL or non-NULL (no nonnull attribute).
n is the number of bytes from str to consider.

functions.name: wget_human_readable
functions.description: Formats the number n into a human-readable string (e.g., using size units) into buf and returns buf.
requirements: buf must point to a writable buffer of at least bufsize bytes.

functions.name: wget_get_screen_size
functions.description: Retrieves the current terminal's screen dimensions in characters.
requirements: width must be a valid pointer to int.
height must be a valid pointer to int.

functions.name: wget_fdgetline
functions.description: Reads a line from file descriptor fd, reallocating *buf as needed, and updates *bufsize. Returns number of bytes read or negative on error.
requirements: buf must be a valid pointer to a char* variable.
bufsize must be a valid pointer to a size_t variable.
fd must be a valid file descriptor.

functions.name: wget_getline
functions.description: Reads a line from stream fp, reallocating *buf as needed, and updates *bufsize. Returns number of bytes read or negative on error.
requirements: buf must be a valid pointer to a char* variable.
bufsize must be a valid pointer to a size_t variable.
fp must be a valid FILE* opened for reading.

functions.name: wget_vpopenf
functions.signature: FILE *wget_vpopenf(const char *type, const char *__restrict fmt, va_list args);
functions.description: Formats a command using fmt/args and opens a pipe to the process with popen-like semantics using mode type (e.g., "r"/"w"). Returns a FILE* or NULL.
requirements: type should be a valid popen mode string (e.g., "r" or "w").
fmt must be a valid printf-style format matching args.

functions.name: wget_popenf
functions.description: Formats a command and opens a pipe to the spawned process using popen-like semantics and mode type. Returns FILE* or NULL.
requirements: type should be a valid popen mode string.
fmt must be a valid printf-style format and the variadic arguments must match.

functions.name: wget_popen2f
functions.description: Spawns a process from a formatted command and opens up to two pipes (input and output). Returns a FILE* (likely one side) or NULL. Exact semantics not fully documented in header.
requirements: If non-NULL, fpin and fpout must be pointers to FILE* variables to receive stream handles.
fmt must be a valid printf-style format and the variadic arguments must match.

functions.name: wget_fd_popen3
functions.signature: pid_t wget_fd_popen3(int *fdin, int *fdout, int *fderr, const char *const *argv);
functions.description: Spawns a process with argv and sets up three pipes using file descriptors for stdin/stdout/stderr. Returns child pid or negative on error.
requirements: argv must point to a NULL-terminated vector of strings suitable for exec().
fdin, fdout, fderr must be valid pointers to int to receive FDs or may be NULL if not needed.

functions.name: wget_popen3
functions.signature: pid_t wget_popen3(FILE **fpin, FILE **fpout, FILE **fperr, const char *const *argv);
functions.description: Spawns a process with argv and opens FILE* streams for stdin/stdout/stderr. Returns child pid or negative on error.
requirements: argv must point to a NULL-terminated vector of strings suitable for exec().
fpin, fpout, fperr must be pointers to FILE* variables to receive streams or may be NULL if not needed.

functions.name: wget_read_file
functions.description: Reads an entire file into a newly allocated buffer and returns it; optionally returns its size via size. Returns NULL on failure.
requirements: fname must be a valid path string.
If size is non-NULL, it must point to a size_t to receive the byte count.
Caller must free the returned buffer with free-compatible function.

functions.name: wget_update_file
functions.signature: int wget_update_file(const char *fname, wget_update_load_fn *load_func, wget_update_save_fn *save_func, void *context);
functions.description: Opens file fname, invokes load_func to read/transform state and save_func to write updated state, using context. Returns status int.
requirements: fname must be a valid path string.
load_func and save_func must be valid function pointers accepting the provided context and FILE*.

functions.name: wget_truncate
functions.description: Truncates or extends a file at path to the given length. Returns 0 on success or negative on error (exact convention not documented).
requirements: path must be a valid path string.

functions.name: wget_local_charset_encoding
functions.description: Returns the name of the local system character set encoding.

functions.name: wget_memiconv
functions.signature: int wget_memiconv(const char *src_encoding, const void *src, size_t srclen, const char *dst_encoding, char **out, size_t *outlen);
functions.description: Converts a memory buffer from src_encoding to dst_encoding, allocating *out and setting *outlen. Returns status int.
requirements: src_encoding and dst_encoding must be valid encoding names.
src must point to at least srclen bytes.
out must be a valid pointer to a char* variable; function allocates *out on success.
outlen must be a valid pointer to size_t to receive output length.

functions.name: wget_striconv
functions.signature: char *wget_striconv(const char *src, const char *src_encoding, const char *dst_encoding);
functions.description: Converts a NUL-terminated string from src_encoding to dst_encoding and returns a newly allocated string or NULL on failure.
requirements: src must be a NUL-terminated string.
src_encoding and dst_encoding must be valid encoding names.
Caller must free returned string.

functions.name: wget_str_needs_encoding
functions.description: Checks whether the given string contains bytes needing percent-encoding (or encoding) according to library rules. Pure.
requirements: s must be a valid NUL-terminated string.

functions.name: wget_str_is_valid_utf8
functions.description: Validates whether the given NUL-terminated string is valid UTF-8. Pure.
requirements: utf8 must be a valid NUL-terminated string.

functions.name: wget_str_to_utf8
functions.description: Converts a string in encoding to UTF-8. Returns newly allocated UTF-8 string or NULL on failure.
requirements: src must be a NUL-terminated string.
encoding must be a valid encoding name.
Caller must free returned string.

functions.name: wget_utf8_to_str
functions.description: Converts a UTF-8 string to the specified encoding. Returns newly allocated string or NULL on failure.
requirements: src must be a NUL-terminated UTF-8 string.
encoding must be a valid encoding name.
Caller must free returned string.

functions.name: wget_str_to_ascii
functions.description: Converts the given string to ASCII representation (e.g., transliteration/escaping). Returns a pointer (lifespan not documented).
requirements: src must be a NUL-terminated string.

functions.name: wget_strlcpy
functions.signature: size_t wget_strlcpy(char *__restrict dst, const char *__restrict src, size_t size);
functions.description: Copies src into dst of size size, NUL-terminating where possible. Returns length of src.
requirements: dst must be a writable buffer of at least size bytes.
src must be a NUL-terminated string.

functions.name: wget_strscpy
functions.signature: ssize_t wget_strscpy(char *__restrict dst, const char *__restrict src, size_t size);
functions.description: Safe string copy into dst of size size; returns number of bytes copied or negative on truncation/error (exact semantics per implementation).
requirements: dst must be a writable buffer of at least size bytes.
src must be a NUL-terminated string.

functions.name: wget_list_append
functions.signature: WGETAPI void * NULLABLE wget_list_append(wget_list **list, const void *data, size_t size)
functions.description: Appends a new element containing a copy of data (size bytes) to the end of a doubly-linked wget_list. Returns a pointer to the stored element or NULL on failure. Typical usage: create or grow a list of items with arbitrary payload.
requirements: list must be a valid pointer to a wget_list* (address of the list variable)
data must be non-NULL (WGET_GCC_NONNULL_ALL on declaration)
size should specify the number of bytes to copy from data; acceptable range not documented
Returned pointer may be NULL on allocation failure; callers should check for NULL before use

functions.name: wget_list_prepend
functions.signature: WGETAPI void * NULLABLE wget_list_prepend(wget_list **list, const void *data, size_t size)
functions.description: Prepends a new element containing a copy of data (size bytes) to the beginning of a wget_list. Returns pointer to stored element or NULL on failure.
requirements: list must be a valid pointer to a wget_list*
data must be non-NULL (WGET_GCC_NONNULL_ALL)
size indicates number of bytes copied from data
Check return for NULL on allocation failure

functions.name: wget_list_getfirst
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the first element’s data in the list, or NULL if the list is empty or list is NULL.
requirements: list may be NULL; returns NULL in that case (no nonnull attribute)
Returned pointer may be NULL; caller must check

functions.name: wget_list_getlast
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the last element’s data in the list, or NULL if empty/NULL.
requirements: list may be NULL; returns NULL if not available
Caller must check for NULL

functions.name: wget_list_getnext
functions.description: Given an element pointer previously obtained from the list, returns the next element’s data pointer, or NULL if there is no next element.
requirements: elem may be NULL; returns NULL
elem must refer to an element belonging to a wget_list (inferred); otherwise behavior is undefined

functions.name: wget_list_remove
functions.description: Removes the specified element from the list. Does not return a value.
requirements: list must be a valid pointer to a wget_list* (WGET_GCC_NONNULL_ALL)
elem must be a valid element pointer belonging to the list (inferred)

functions.name: wget_list_free
functions.description: Frees the entire list and sets the list pointer to NULL (inferred from double-pointer pattern).
requirements: list must be a valid pointer to a wget_list* (WGET_GCC_NONNULL_ALL)
After return, *list may be set to NULL; caller must not use previous element pointers

functions.name: wget_list_browse
functions.signature: WGETAPI int wget_list_browse(const wget_list *list, wget_list_browse_fn *browse, void *context)
functions.description: Iterates over all elements in the list, invoking the user callback for each element. Returns the callback’s last return value or 0 if list or browse is NULL (inferred from similar map browse docs).
requirements: browse must be non-NULL (WGET_GCC_NONNULL((2)))
list may be NULL; behavior of returning 0 inferred but not guaranteed for list (header note was for stringmap/hashmap)
Callback must tolerate the provided context pointer (may be NULL)

functions.name: wget_memdup
functions.signature: WGETAPI void * NULLABLE wget_memdup(const void *m, size_t n)
functions.description: Allocates a new buffer and copies n bytes from m into it. Returns pointer to new memory or NULL on failure.
requirements: m must be non-NULL (WGET_GCC_NONNULL_ALL)
n is the number of bytes to copy; if n is 0, behavior is implementation-defined (unknown)
Caller must free the returned buffer with wget_free()/free as appropriate

functions.name: wget_strdup
functions.description: Allocates and returns a duplicate of the NUL-terminated string s, or NULL on allocation failure.
requirements: s must be a valid pointer to a NUL-terminated string (no explicit NONNULL in declaration; typical requirement)
Caller must free the returned string

functions.name: wget_strmemdup
functions.signature: WGETAPI char * NULLABLE wget_strmemdup(const void *m, size_t n)
functions.description: Allocates a new NUL-terminated string and copies n bytes from m, appending a terminating NUL. Returns the new string or NULL on failure.
requirements: m must be a valid pointer to at least n bytes
Caller must free the returned string

functions.name: wget_strmemcpy
functions.signature: WGETAPI size_t wget_strmemcpy(char *__restrict s, size_t ssize, const void *__restrict m, size_t n)
functions.description: Copies up to n bytes from m into s, respecting destination capacity ssize. Returns the number of bytes written (exact semantics not fully documented).
requirements: s must point to a buffer of at least ssize bytes
m must point to at least n bytes
ssize must reflect the size of s; behavior if n > ssize is implementation-specific (unknown)

functions.name: wget_strmemcpy_a
functions.signature: WGETAPI void * NULLABLE wget_strmemcpy_a(char *s, size_t ssize, const void *m, size_t n)
functions.description: Like wget_strmemcpy but marked nonnull for all args and returns a pointer (possibly to end or to s). If allocation occurs internally is unknown. Returns a pointer or NULL on failure.
requirements: s, m must be non-NULL (WGET_GCC_NONNULL_ALL)
ssize must be the capacity of s and should be >= n (exact requirement unspecified)
Caller must check return for NULL

functions.name: wget_base64_is_string
functions.description: Checks if src looks like a valid Base64-encoded string. Returns true if valid.
requirements: src must be a valid NUL-terminated string

functions.name: wget_base64_get_decoded_length
functions.description: Computes the maximum decoded byte length for a Base64 input of length len.
requirements: len is the length of the Base64 input in bytes; must fit in size_t

functions.name: wget_base64_get_encoded_length
functions.description: Computes the maximum Base64-encoded length for a binary input of length len (not including NUL terminator).
requirements: len is the length of the binary input in bytes

functions.name: wget_base64_decode
functions.signature: WGETAPI size_t wget_base64_decode(char *__restrict dst, const char *__restrict src, size_t n)

functions.name: wget_base64_encode
functions.signature: WGETAPI size_t wget_base64_encode(char *__restrict dst, const char *__restrict src, size_t n)

dst must have enough capacity; use wget_base64_get_encoded_length(n) to size

functions.name: wget_base64_urlencode
functions.signature: WGETAPI size_t wget_base64_urlencode(char *__restrict dst, const char *__restrict src, size_t n)
functions.description: Encodes n bytes from src to URL-safe Base64 into dst. Returns number of bytes written.
requirements: dst, src must be non-NULL (WGET_GCC_NONNULL_ALL)
dst must have enough capacity; size calculation similar to Base64 encoded length

functions.name: wget_base64_decode_alloc

functions.name: wget_base64_encode_alloc
functions.signature: WGETAPI char * NULLABLE wget_base64_encode_alloc(const char *src, size_t n)
functions.description: Allocates a buffer, encodes n bytes from src to Base64, returns the NUL-terminated encoded string or NULL on failure.
requirements: src must be non-NULL (WGET_GCC_NONNULL_ALL)
Caller must free the returned string

functions.name: wget_base64_encode_vprintf_alloc
functions.signature: WGETAPI char * NULLABLE wget_base64_encode_vprintf_alloc(const char *__restrict fmt, va_list args)

functions.name: wget_base64_encode_printf_alloc
functions.signature: WGETAPI char * NULLABLE wget_base64_encode_printf_alloc(const char *__restrict fmt, ...)

Caller must free returned string
Variadic arguments must match fmt

functions.name: wget_bitmap_init

functions.name: wget_bitmap_free

requirements: bitmap must be a valid pointer to wget_bitmap*

functions.name: wget_bitmap_set
functions.description: Sets the bit at index n in the bitmap.
requirements: bitmap must be a valid initialized bitmap
n is a zero-based index; must be within the allocated range (not explicitly documented)

functions.name: wget_bitmap_clear

requirements: bitmap must be a valid initialized bitmap
n must be within range (not documented)

functions.name: wget_bitmap_get
functions.signature: WGETAPI bool wget_bitmap_get(const wget_bitmap *bitmap, unsigned n)
functions.description: Returns true if the bit at index n is set; false otherwise.
requirements: bitmap must be a valid initialized bitmap
n must be within range (not documented)

functions.name: wget_buffer_init
functions.signature: WGETAPI int wget_buffer_init(wget_buffer *buf, char *data, size_t size)

requirements: buf must be non-NULL (WGET_GCC_NONNULL((1)))

Caller must check return value

functions.name: wget_buffer_alloc
functions.description: Allocates a wget_buffer with an internal buffer of at least size bytes. Returns a non-NULL pointer or terminates depending on allocator attributes; header marks RETURNS_NONNULL for some builds.
requirements: size is the initial capacity
Caller must free with wget_buffer_free()

functions.name: wget_buffer_ensure_capacity
functions.description: Ensures the buffer has capacity for at least size bytes; may reallocate. Returns 0 on success, nonzero on failure (inferred).
requirements: buf must be a valid buffer
Caller should check return value before writing

functions.name: wget_buffer_deinit
functions.description: Releases internal resources of a buffer initialized with wget_buffer_init; does not free the wget_buffer struct itself (inferred).
requirements: buf must be non-NULL (WGET_GCC_NONNULL((1)))
After deinit, using buf’s data without reinit is invalid

functions.name: wget_buffer_free
functions.description: Frees a buffer allocated by wget_buffer_alloc and sets pointer to NULL.
requirements: buf must be a valid pointer to wget_buffer*
After return, *buf is invalid (likely NULL)

functions.name: wget_buffer_free_data
functions.description: Frees only the internal data of the buffer if owned, leaving the structure allocated.
requirements: buf must be a valid buffer

functions.name: wget_buffer_reset
functions.description: Resets buffer length to zero and optionally clears error flags; capacity is retained (inferred).
requirements: buf must be a valid buffer

functions.name: wget_buffer_memcpy

data must point to at least length bytes

functions.name: wget_buffer_memcat

requirements: buf must be valid
data must point to at least length bytes

functions.name: wget_buffer_strcpy

requirements: buf must be valid
s must be a valid NUL-terminated string

functions.name: wget_buffer_strcat
functions.description: Appends the NUL-terminated string s to the buffer. Returns number of bytes appended.
requirements: buf must be valid
s must be a valid NUL-terminated string

functions.name: wget_buffer_bufcpy
functions.description: Copies the contents of src into buf, replacing previous content. Returns number of bytes written.
requirements: buf and src must be valid buffers

functions.name: wget_buffer_bufcat

requirements: buf and src must be valid buffers

functions.name: wget_buffer_memset

functions.name: wget_buffer_memset_append

requirements: buf must be valid

functions.name: wget_buffer_trim
functions.description: Trims leading/trailing whitespace from buffer content in place and returns a pointer to the internal data.
requirements: buf must be valid

functions.name: wget_buffer_vprintf_append

args must be valid va_list

requirements: buf and fmt must be non-NULL (WGET_GCC_PRINTF_FORMAT)
Variadic args must match fmt

functions.name: wget_vasprintf

fmt must be non-NULL

functions.name: wget_aprintf
functions.signature: WGETAPI char * NULLABLE wget_aprintf(const char *__restrict fmt, ...)

Variadic args must match fmt

fmt must be non-NULL

args must be valid va_list

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Generator for arbitrary NUL-terminated strings suitable for libwget string APIs.
# We craft inputs that exercise comparisons, UTF-8 validation, Base64 detection,
# content-encoding name lookup, and IP family detection.
# The fuzzer harness will call FUZZ_PARAM_STR multiple times; our single buffer
# will be split by the harness framework. We therefore include multiple strings
# separated by newlines. Each line is a distinct interesting case.

_MAX_TOTAL = 4096

def _rand_ascii(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # Mix of printable ASCII including separators and punctuation
    alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + string.punctuation + ' \t'
    return ''.join(r.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))

def _rand_bytes(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    n = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return bytes(r.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))

def _valid_utf8_bytes(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    # Build a mix of ASCII and valid multi-byte UTF-8 sequences
    out = bytearray()
    target = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    while len(out) < target:
        choice = r.random()
        if choice < 0.6:
            out.append(r.randint(0x20, 0x7E))
        elif choice < 0.8:
            # 2-byte sequence
            b1 = r.randint(0xC2, 0xDF)
            b2 = r.randint(0x80, 0xBF)
            out.extend([b1, b2])
        elif choice < 0.95:
            # 3-byte
            b1 = r.randint(0xE0, 0xEF)
            if b1 == 0xE0:
                b2 = r.randint(0xA0, 0xBF)
            elif b1 == 0xED:
                b2 = r.randint(0x80, 0x9F)
            else:
                b2 = r.randint(0x80, 0xBF)
            b3 = r.randint(0x80, 0xBF)
            out.extend([b1, b2, b3])
        else:
            # 4-byte
            b1 = r.randint(0xF0, 0xF4)
            if b1 == 0xF0:
                b2 = r.randint(0x90, 0xBF)
            elif b1 == 0xF4:
                b2 = r.randint(0x80, 0x8F)
            else:
                b2 = r.randint(0x80, 0xBF)
            b3 = r.randint(0x80, 0xBF)
            b4 = r.randint(0x80, 0xBF)
            out.extend([b1, b2, b3, b4])
    return bytes(out[:target])

def _base64_like(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int, urlsafe: bool = False, with_pad: bool = True) -> str:
    alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + ("-_" if urlsafe else "+/")
    # length close to a multiple of 4 to look valid
    n = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    n = max(0, n - (n % 4)) or 4
    s = ''.join(r.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))
    if with_pad:
        pad = r.randint(0, 2)
        if pad:
            s = s[:-pad] + ("=" * pad)
    return s

def _ip_like(r: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    # IPv4, IPv6 compressed/expanded, hostnames
    parts = []
    # IPv4
    parts.append("%d.%d.%d.%d" % (r.randint(0,255), r.randint(0,255), r.randint(0,255), r.randint(0,255)))
    # Hostname
    labels = [ _rand_ascii(r, 1, r.randint(2,6)).lower().replace(' ', '') for _ in range(r.randint(2,4)) ]
    labels = [ (''.join(ch for ch in lb if ch.isalnum() or ch=='-') or 'a') for lb in labels ]
    parts.append('.'.join(labels))
    # IPv6 compressed
    hexd = [format(r.randint(0, 0xFFFF), 'x') for _ in range(6)]
    parts.append(":".join(hexd[:3]) + "::" + ":".join(hexd[3:]))
    # IPv6 full
    parts.append(":".join(format(r.randint(0, 0xFFFF), 'x') for _ in range(8)))
    return parts

def _http_header_tokens(r: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    # For comparison and token predicates
    return [
        "Content-Type",
        "content-type",
        "CONTENT-TYPE",
        "gzip",
        "GZip",
        "deflate",
        "br",
        "zstd",
        "application/json; charset=UTF-8",
        "text/html; charset=iso-8859-1",
        ",;=()<>@:/[]?{}\\\"'\t ",  # separators and punctuation
    ]

def _encoding_names() -> List[str]:
    return [
        "gzip", "deflate", "br", "brotli", "zstd", "xz", "lzma", "bzip2", "identity", "unknown",
        "GZIP", "Deflate", "Br", "ZSTD"
    ]

def _uris(r: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    hosts = _ip_like(r)
    return [
        f"http://{hosts[1]}/",
        f"https://{hosts[1]}/path/To/File?Q=1&x=Y#frag",
        f"http://[{hosts[2]}]/res%20path?q=a+b",
    ]

def _cases_for_compare(r: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    # Pairs will be pulled sequentially by FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls
    return [
        "",  # empty
        "",  # empty
        "abc",
        "abc",
        "Case",
        "case",
        "caf\xc3\xa9",  # UTF-8
        "CAF\xc3\x89",
        _rand_ascii(r, 1, 32),
        _rand_ascii(r, 1, 32),
    ]

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    lines: List[bytes] = []

    # Comparison-focused cases (consumed as pairs)
    for s in _cases_for_compare(r):
        lines.append(s.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore'))

    # Base64-looking and non-base64 strings
    lines.append(_base64_like(r, 4, 64, urlsafe=False, with_pad=True).encode('ascii'))
    lines.append(_base64_like(r, 4, 64, urlsafe=True, with_pad=False).encode('ascii'))
    lines.append(_rand_ascii(r, 5, 25).replace('=', 'x').encode('ascii'))

    # Valid and invalid UTF-8
    lines.append(_valid_utf8_bytes(r, 1, 40))
    bad = bytearray(_valid_utf8_bytes(r, 4, 20))
    # Corrupt a continuation byte to make invalid UTF-8
    if bad:
        idx = r.randrange(len(bad))
        bad[idx] = r.randint(0x00, 0x1F)
    lines.append(bytes(bad))

    # Encoding names for wget_content_encoding_by_name
    for name in _encoding_names():
        lines.append(name.encode('ascii'))

    # Hosts for wget_ip_is_family
    for h in _ip_like(r):
        lines.append(h.encode('ascii'))

    # HTTP-like tokens/headers
    for t in _http_header_tokens(r):
        lines.append(t.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore'))

    # URIs
    for u in _uris(r):
        lines.append(u.encode('utf-8'))

    # Random raw bytes chunks to exercise arbitrary string consumers
    for _ in range(3):
        lines.append(_rand_bytes(r, 0, 64))

    # Ensure non-empty and within limit; join with newlines so each FUZZ_PARAM_STR() gets a distinct line
    blob = b"\n".join(lines)
    if len(blob) > _MAX_TOTAL:
        blob = blob[:_MAX_TOTAL]
    return blob
